title: Pool.acquire() under genuine multi-OS-thread contention loses row-lock isolation (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims collide across threads)
summary: While writing genuine multi-connection concurrency tests for ORD-01 AC1 and ORD-04 AC1 (WF02-batch-2-20260811, TEST-DESIGNER step), found that when multiple std.Thread.spawn-created OS threads each call bpm.pool.Pool.acquire() (and subsequently conn.begin()) concurrently on a shared *Pool, and then race a FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim query, the row-lock isolation SKIP LOCKED is supposed to guarantee across connections breaks down: all 8 racing threads observed claiming the exact same row, which should be impossible under PostgreSQL's row-locking semantics. Confirmed NOT a client-side aliasing bug (distinct *Conn pointers, distinct pg_backend_pid() values, distinct per-thread memory addresses for the returned correlation_id). An equivalent test in plain Python (real threading.Thread + psycopg2, identical BEGIN + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED query, identical barrier synchronization) correctly produced exactly one winner every time, ruling out a PostgreSQL server-side or environment-level cause. Isolating the variable -- pre-acquiring and begin()-ing all 8 connections sequentially from the main test thread BEFORE spawning any racing thread, so only the claim query itself races across threads -- reliably reproduced the correct one-winner result (confirmed clean across 6+ consecutive runs).

root_cause.details: src/db/pool.zig's Pool.acquire() (and/or a callee such as applyRequestStorageRouting) is suspected unsafe when called concurrently from raw std.Thread.spawn-created OS threads. The shared std.testing.io / Io.Threaded instance (Zig 0.16's async-IO runtime) is designed as a cooperative task scheduler over its own bounded worker-thread pool; it is plausible that driving it reentrantly from external raw OS threads (rather than through its own task-spawning API) produces incorrect behavior under contention -- e.g. misdelivering a completed I/O response to the wrong logical caller. Pool.acquire()'s own mutex (std.Io.Mutex, backed by real atomic CAS via cmpxchgStrong) was checked and ruled out as the cause -- it correctly serializes the idle-connection-list bookkeeping regardless of caller thread origin. The bug's precise location within Pool.acquire()'s call chain has not yet been pinpointed; this issue records the empirical isolation (acquire-time contention vs. query-time contention) for whoever picks this up next, not a full root-cause diagnosis.

prevention: Write a minimal standalone repro isolating Pool.acquire() alone (no ordering query) called concurrently from N raw threads, to confirm/refute whether the bug is in acquire() itself vs. something interacting with the subsequent query.
Audit Io.Threaded's documented contract for whether it supports being invoked from external OS threads at all, vs. only from tasks it spawns itself.

If Io.Threaded is not safe under raw-thread reentrancy, Pool.acquire() (or its callers) may need an explicit mutex/serialization point around the whole acquire+first-query sequence when called from raw threads, or Pool needs to document/enforce that callers must not invoke it from threads Io.Threaded does not manage.

Any future test needing genuine multi-thread concurrency against a shared *Pool should pre-acquire (and begin(), where a transaction is needed) all connections sequentially from the spawning thread BEFORE spawning the racing threads, matching the workaround in tests/integration/ordering_consumer_test.zig's TC-ORD-01-AC1-concurrent and TC-ORD-04-AC1-concurrent, until this is fixed.
